data.narrative:
Cognition is a Series A artificial intelligence and software company founded by Scott Wu, Steven Hao, and Walden Yan that has raised over $400M. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 peers—1 public (Palantir) and 8 private companies—operating in the AI & Software sector at the same or adjacent funding stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using total raised ($400M+) as a proxy base and applying a typical 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier, implied a valuation of $9M. The peer-median approach examined five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Reflection AI ($25.0B), Scale AI ($29.0B), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B), Black Forest Labs ($3.2B), and Field AI ($2.0B). The median across this set was $5.6B, with a range spanning $2.0B to $29.0B.

The triangulated analysis across both methods suggests a valuation range of $8M to $6.4B, with a median of $2.8B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty in the frontier AI sector, where stage-alone progression methods produce valuations orders of magnitude below peer comparables. The key uncertainty centers on whether Cognition's product-market position and revenue trajectory more closely resemble lower-end peers like Field AI or upper-tier names like Scale AI and Reflection AI. Capital deployed ($400M+) exceeds the stage-progression floor substantially, suggesting the higher end of the range merits closer scrutiny.
